messages:
Mira Chen: Heads up — after landing int4 kernels for rwd-model-2.1 on canary we see a regression in zh/ja translation quality, plus weird deletions when Arabic/RTL spans join CJK.
Kai Patel: Oof, can you paste a repro?
Mira Chen: Repro snippets below. note the token stream shows a missing subtoken between CJK chars when an RTL mark is adjacent.
Mira Chen: ```
# src sentence (zh): 这是 一个 测试
# model output (canary int4): 这是一个 测试   <-- extra spacing? missing middle subtoken
# tokenized (tokenizer_v2): ["▁这", "是", "▁一个", "▁测试"]
# tokenized (runtime int4 path): ["▁这", "▁测试"]  <-- middle tokens dropped
```
Jordan Li: That's alarming. Could be a faulty KV cache index or a tokenizer merge table mismatch after the quantized load. Any diffs in tokenizer.json between prod and canary? :thinking_face:
Mira Chen: I diffed them — the files are identical, but the runtime loader prints this on startup: `Warning: tokenizer merges not applied for optimized_kernel_v3` (only in int4 runtime).
Alice Gomez: Maybe the quantized kernels use a different byte alignment and we have an off-by-one in the token id mapping when converting to int16 before packing. I've seen similar where embedding lookup index wraps.
Kai Patel: Quick check: can you run the token-diff tool with the same seed on CPU decode vs canary int4? Command: `tools/token-diff --model rwd-model-2.1 --input "这是一个测试" --compare cpu,canary-int4 --dump-tokens`.
Mira Chen: Ran it, attaching minimal output: ```
CPU tokens: [0x12,0x45,0x22,0x7f]
CANARY tokens: [0x12,0x00,0x7f]
Mapping: 0x45 -> 0x00 (dropped)
```
Jordan Li: 0x00 is reserved for padding/unk in our runtime — that explains the deletion. So something is mapping valid ids to 0 during kernel translation.
Alice Gomez: Also saw small RTL-specific effect: when input contains Arabic merging marks (e.g., "ـ"), the tokenization boundary moves and then the int4 path drops the intervening token. Likely a side effect of vectorized token id packing assuming L-to-R layout.
Mira Chen: Impact metrics: BLEU down ~4.8 on zh->en testset, chrF -3.2. RTL lang (ar->en) has sentence-level deletions ~0.6% increased.
Kai Patel: Proposed mitigation: roll back int4 canary, mark as hotfix, then bisect kernel commit that introduced `pack_token_ids` optimization. Also add unit test using mixed-direction inputs.
Mira Chen: Agreed. I've rolled canary back to int8 on the canary cluster and alerted infra. deploy-bot: "Model rwd-model-2.1 canary reverted to int8 at 2025-11-18T14:21:18Z"
deploy-bot: "Canary health: degraded -> healthy (after revert)."
Jordan Li: Next steps: (1) create a minimal failing test in repo (2) run bisect on kernel commits between v2.0.11 and v2.1.0-optpack (3) add tokenizer-id-consistency assert in runtime loader.
Alice Gomez: I'll own the bisect and add the assert. Mira — can you upload failing examples to /evals/multilang/cjk_rtl_failcases.txt and include the exact environment (cuda driver, cudnn)?
Mira Chen: Uploaded files and env: `cuda 12.1, cudnn 9.0, driver 545.67`. Link: https://internal/redwood/evals/cjk_rtl_failcases.txt
Kai Patel: Thanks. Also let's add a quick smoke to the canary pipeline that runs `tools/token-diff` on a small mixed-script set before promoting. If that passes, we won't regress silently.
Mira Chen: Sounds good. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. I'll follow up with a short PR for the test. :white_check_mark:
